"Madhav, the dispatch note needs Friday's date, not today's," said Zainab, tapping the file. "The client expects it went out on time."

"I can't put Friday, ma'am. The truck left today."

"Then what do I tell them?"

"Let me write a note saying the truck was delayed by two days and why. The client sees the reason, and our record stays true."

"It'll look bad."

"A clear note looks better than a wrong date they may catch later. I can have it ready this afternoon, with the driver's message attached."

Zainab was silent, then pushed the file across. "Fine. Bring it by four."

Madhav nodded and pushed his chair back, already reaching for a pen.

qa.q: By what time did Zainab ask for the note?
qa.a: She asked for it by four.

qa.q: What is Madhav feeling as he says a clear note looks better than a wrong date?
qa.a: Madhav feels firm and calm but wants to help, offering a solution rather than just saying no.

qa.q: What could Madhav do if Zainab had refused the note, and why?
qa.a: Madhav could ask to speak with a senior about how such delays are usually reported, because the aim is to keep the record true while solving the client's worry.

qa.q: How might Zainab see Madhav's offer?
qa.a: Zainab may feel relieved to have a workable answer for the client, even though she first heard the refusal as a problem.

grounding: The employee says the paper cannot be backdated but offers to write a note explaining the delay that afternoon.

passage:
I'm Jasleen. In my fourth month at a small export firm, my manager, Yamini, came to my desk at eleven, stressed. The buyer's inspection certificate had come late, and she wanted me to put last week's date on our dispatch approval so the file 'looked clean' for the buyer's audit.
I'd already decided I wouldn't backdate anything. But I also knew a flat no would leave her stuck with a real problem.
So I said it in steps. 'Ma'am, I can't put an earlier date on the approval. It has to show when we actually approved it. But the buyer's real worry is the delay, right? I can write a short note today explaining why the certificate came late, what we did and when it was cleared, with the courier receipt attached. I'll have it ready by three.'
She was quiet for a second, then nodded. 'Do that.'
At 2:40 I sent it. The buyer's auditor replied the next day: 'Noted, thank you for the explanation.'

qa.q: By what time did Jasleen offer to have the note ready?
Why did Jasleen not just give a flat no?
qa.a: Jasleen felt for Yamini's stress and wanted to help solve the real problem, not leave her stuck.
It met the buyer's real need, an explanation of the delay, while keeping the record true.

qa.q: How might Yamini feel when the buyer's auditor replies?
qa.a: Relieved, and perhaps grateful that the honest note worked better than the shortcut she asked for.

grounding: Shows an employee refusing to backdate an approval but offering a same-day note explaining the delay, which meets the manager's real need.

Senior accountant's note, 19 September. Usha, finance shared services.
I'm recording what I overheard this morning, with Nandini's permission, because I think it was handled well.
Our section manager asked Nandini, who joined in March, to change the date on a vendor invoice approval to last month, so it would fall inside the closed quarter. He said the regional office wanted the numbers 'tidy' by noon.
Nandini didn't argue. She said, 'I can't change the approval date, sir. But I can prepare a short adjustment note showing it belongs to this quarter, with the reason, so regional office sees exactly what happened. I'll have it in forty minutes.'
He paused, then told her to go ahead. The note went out at 11:30. Regional office accepted it without further questions.
Afterwards Nandini came to my desk, hands still a little unsteady, and asked if she had done the right thing. I told her she had solved his actual problem without breaking a rule.

qa.q: How long did Nandini say the note would take?
What do Nandini's unsteady hands afterwards suggest?
qa.a: She was nervous about refusing a manager and unsure she had done right, even though she stayed calm in the moment.

qa.q: What else could Nandini do if this kind of request comes again?
qa.a: Offer the same honest alternative, and keep a note of the request in case it needs taking further.

qa.q: How does the morning look to Usha, who wrote the note?
qa.a: Usha sees a new employee turn a pressured request into a lawful fix, and reassures her afterwards.

grounding: Shows an employee declining to backdate an approval and offering an explanatory note the same morning, which meets the manager's need.
